doc.title: Jimmy Cobb — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Drinkert versus Schroeder and Walter Booker
summary: Cobb separates Carl Drinkert from Carl Schroeder, and mentions Booker's home studio.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Just to throw something out, you said the end it was – you mentioned Drinkert. But that’s – I think you talked about him earlier with Billie Holiday. So was it Drinkert, then Schroeder, or?
No, Drinkert was first. Drinkert’s when I was still in Washington. Schroeder’s after I left and went through all this stuff with Miles.
Schroeder’s at the end of Sarah.
Yeah, we’re talking ’50s – we’re talking about ’40s and ’70s. That’s the difference in that.
Bookie. Did you bring him into that, into the group?

Yeah. I don’t know. He got in there. I think he might have knew – he might have been with – he knew Sarah too, because Bookie had a place in his apartment where we used to make recordings all night. You can build yourself a little home studio. So everybody used to come through there. I’m sure that at one time or another Sass was up there. Everybody used to come through. We used to sit down and party and make records all night, with John Hicks, everybody.

Let’s cut, and let’s come back, and I want you to pick up with, when we come back, pick up with your relationship with Walter Booker, where that begins, how that evolves, and then talk about this scene that I didn’t know about and probably a lot of people don’t know about.
